kernel_of_truth: The dome is right that a total solar eclipse perturbs the geomagnetic field, and on 2026-08-12 the raw H-component at its named stations really did sit 13-19 nT below quiet-day levels during the eclipse window — squarely in the dome's stated range for two stations. That is a real observation, not noise. It fails as a dome confirmation because the same depression was present 14:00-16:00 UT, before first contact anywhere in Europe, matches a storm-recovery Dst offset of ~12-15 nT, and its sharpest dips (17:09, 18:47 UT) are simultaneous from Portugal to Romania instead of following the shadow. Remove the offset and the eclipse-attributable signal is within ~5 nT of zero.
